issues.message: The Modelica parameter is set to 10.0 s, but the SysML contract also contains an explicit updated requirement for the wait after Tank 1 high to be 12.0 s (e.g. REQ-0156 / REQ-0033 / CR-004 evidence). The implementation therefore encodes the superseded timing rather than the approved one.
The Modelica parameter is set to 10.0 s, but the SysML contract includes an approved update requiring 12.0 s after Tank 1 low before the next action (e.g. REQ-0110 / REQ-0159 / CON-0042).
The Modelica parameter is set to 10.0 s, but the SysML contract includes an approved update requiring 8.0 s after Tank 2 low before the next fill starts (e.g. REQ-0111 / REQ-0160 / CON-0043).

The Modelica parameter is 0.78 m, but the SysML contract includes an approved effective T1 high limit of 0.80 m / 0.8 m in the later requirements and change approval (e.g. REQ-0047, REQ-0155, REQ-0162, REQ-0033/CR-004 evidence). The implemented value reflects the older baseline, not the current contract.

The Modelica parameter is 0.8 m, which matches the approved high-level setpoint. However, the model does not actually encode the contract’s explicit transition/guard behavior or assertions anywhere—only a parameter value is present. The required logic to act on the threshold is missing from equations/algorithm/assertions.

The parameter value matches 10.0 s, but the contract expects this to be implemented as active controller logic (wait then open V2) and not just as a stored parameter. No corresponding equation, algorithm, assertion, or state machine behavior is implemented in the generated Modelica.

The parameter value matches 10.0 s, but the contract expects active controller behavior (wait then open V3) rather than a passive parameter only. The generated Modelica contains no equation/algorithm/assertion implementing this behavior.

The parameter value matches 10.0 s, but the contract expects this delay to drive the automatic return to Tank 1 filling. The generated Modelica does not implement the corresponding state transition or timer logic.

The contract maps PLC-101 / tankController to a sequence controller with START/STOP/SHUT edge handling, stored interrupted state, timer freeze/resume, priority rules, and valve interlocks. The generated Modelica model is an empty stub and does not implement any of this required behavior in equations, algorithms, or assertions.

LT-101 is required to represent an active level measurement with specified mapping/range behavior. The generated Modelica model is an empty stub and contains no measurement equations, signal mapping, or parameterization implementing the contract.

LT-102 is required to represent an active level measurement with specified mapping/range behavior. The generated Modelica model is an empty stub and contains no measurement equations, signal mapping, or parameterization implementing the contract.

The SysML architecture includes the tanks, valves, sensors, controller, and their physical/signal connections, plus required behaviors such as valve actuation, level dynamics, and command interlocks. The generated Modelica model is only a stub and does not implement these behaviors or connections beyond comments.

This parameter is set to 'allowed', but the contract distinguishes normal operation from SHUT mode: simultaneous V2/V3 open is not allowed during normal automatic operation and is only waived in SHUTDOWN. Encoding a blanket 'allowed' value loses that semantic condition.

The contract contains a required START-from-PAUSED/STOP resume behavior and a stopped-state edge semantics for the TankDemo_Rev12 model, but the generated Modelica encodes this as a numeric placeholder parameter without any governing behavior or bound value. The mapped behavior is not actually implemented.

The contract contains STOP-edge semantics for the TankDemo_Rev12 model, but the generated Modelica encodes this as a numeric placeholder parameter without any governing behavior or bound value. The mapped behavior is not actually implemented.
